findings.title: Unauthenticated user feedback listing exposes partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET returned HTTP 200 with 8 feedback records (fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; no email field). Emails appear only inside comment text, and only in masked form: e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Anonymous records show '(anonymous)'. No complete author email address is disclosed, so the stated confirmation criterion ('emails are present') is not cleanly met. The response does leak the domain and partial local-part fragments of author emails without authentication, which is a weak PII exposure; the Coordinator should decide whether to treat it as a finding or as a low-severity note.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) via /rest/basket/:id — acct2 reads acct1's basket
findings.response_evidence: Acct2 (own_basket_id=7) requested acct1's own basket 6 and got HTTP 200: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. Acct1's own_basket_id is 6, so this is another user's basket with a seeded item (Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3). Basket 1 (UserId 1, not acct1's basket) was also returned with HTTP 200 to acct2: Apple Juice (1000ml) x2, Orange Juice (1000ml) x3, Eggfruit Juice (500ml) x1. Note: basket 1 is owned by UserId 1, not acct1, so the acct1-specific proof comes from basket 6. Object-level authorization on basket IDs is not enforced.

findings.title: CSRF on DVWA security-level change (POST /security.php) — user_token enforced
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php (session dvwa_admin) form: security=high, seclev_submit=Submit (no user_token, no Referer)
findings.response_evidence: Tokenless POST returned 302 to security.php. Follow-up GET shows the page body with the flash message "CSRF token is incorrect" and "Security level is currently: high". The level was already high before this request, so the POST did not change it. The token check fired, so the security-level change is not accepted without a valid user_token. Caveat: no positive control was run (budget cap), so the 302 is interpreted from the rejection message. Level left at high.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing exposes author identifiers with masked emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without authentication, 8 records. No email field is returned; emails only appear inside comment text and are partially masked, e.g. {\"UserId\":1,\"id\":1,\"comment\":\"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)\",...}, {\"UserId\":2,...\"(***@juice-sh.op)\"}, {\"UserId\":3,...\"(***der@juice-sh.op)\"}, {\"UserId\":21,...\"(***ereum@juice-sh.op)\"}. Remaining records show \"UserId\":null with \"(anonymous)\". Emails are masked (local part replaced by ***), so full author email addresses are not disclosed. Partial masking with the domain and fragments of local part does not meet the full-PII disclosure criterion; classified inconclusive per assignment.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing exposes user-linked feedback comments with partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without any authentication, body {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]}. Fields per record: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. No email field is returned as a separate attribute. Comments carry masked author emails: e.g. id=1 "(***in@juice-sh.op)", id=2 "(***@juice-sh.op)", id=3 "(***der@juice-sh.op)", id=4 "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; anonymous records show "(anonymous)" with UserId null. Numeric UserId values (1, 2, 3, 21) are exposed for authenticated-author records. Verdict rationale: the endpoint is genuinely unauthenticated and discloses numeric user IDs plus partially masked email fragments (domain fully visible, local part mostly obscured). The full author email address is NOT disclosed, so the strict CONFIRM criterion ('disclose author email addresses') is not met. This is a partial PII/information-exposure weakness; Coordinator should decide whether to treat as a low-severity CWE-359 instance or reject.

findings.title: Broken object-level authorization on GET /api/Users/{id}: customer acct2 reads acct1's user record
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/whoami as juiceshop_acct1 -> {"user":{}} (no id exposed; email acct1_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id 6)
GET http://juiceshop:3000/api/Users/23 as juiceshop_acct2 (baseline: own record)
findings.response_evidence: juiceshop_acct2 GET /api/Users/22 -> HTTP 200: {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":{\"id\":22,\"username\":\"\",\"email\":\"acct1_bench@juiceshop.local\",\"role\":\"customer\",\"lastLoginIp\":\"0.0.0.0\",\"isActive\":true,\"createdAt\":\"2026-11-13T18:13:47.228Z\",...}}. This is Account 1's record, which acct2 should not be able to read. Baseline juiceshop_acct2 GET /api/Users/23 -> 200 with its own email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local (id 23). Control unauth GET /api/Users/22 -> 401 credentials_required. So any authenticated customer can read other users' records by ID; unauthenticated access is blocked, but cross-user authorization is missing. Note: the list GET /api/Users/ as acct2 also returned all users (HTTP 200), a related exposure. Only the user record (id, email, role) was verified; the basket item check belongs to the separate BOLA item.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback records exposing masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: [session=unauth] HTTP 200, application/json: {"status":"success","data":[...8 records]}. Records returned without any authentication. Fields: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; no email field. Emails appear only inside comment text and are masked by the application: "(***in@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 1), "(***@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 2), "(***der@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 3), "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 21). Records 5-8 have UserId null and author "(anonymous)". Verdict rationale: the endpoint is unauthenticated and leaks author linkage (UserId) and partial email fragments, but full author email addresses are NOT disclosed (masked with ***). The CWE-359 criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is therefore not met in full; partial/masked disclosure only. Unauthenticated access to the feedback data itself is confirmed (CWE-200 candidate).

findings.title: Cross-user access to user record via GET /api/Users/{id} (BOLA) - consistency re-check of existing finding juiceshop:GET:/api/Users/22:CWE-639:99236c4434
findings.response_evidence: [acct2 request] HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":{"id":22,"username":"","email":"acct1_bench@juiceshop.local","role":"customer",...,"createdAt":"2026-11-13T18:13:47.228Z",...}} - acct2 (own basket_id 7) received acct1's user record (acct1 email, id 22). [acct1 control] HTTP 200 identical record for id 22 (acct1 own basket_id 6). Consistent with existing confirmed finding; acct2 is not the owner of user 22 yet receives its data.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user record GET /api/Users/1 (email disclosure) - not reproducible
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 401 {"error":{"message":"No Authorization header was found","name":"UnauthorizedError","code":"credentials_required","status":401}}. No user record returned without credentials, so no unauthenticated disclosure of another user's email. Rejected; the CWE-284/CWE-359 hypothesis does not hold for the unauthenticated context. Authenticated BOLA on /api/Users/{id} was already handled separately and was not re-tested here.

findings.title: GET /rest/user/whoami unauthenticated identity disclosure - not reproducible
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 body: {"user":{}}. Without a session the endpoint discloses no email, id, or identity; the user object is empty. Behavior matches the observation and does not meet the criterion of disclosing user email or identity without a valid session. Rejected.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via /api/Feedbacks (author email disclosure) - not reproduced
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, application/json, unauthenticated. Returned 8 records with fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. No email field exists. Comments carry only masked author emails: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; the remaining entries show "(anonymous)" with UserId null. No unmasked email address appears in any record. Criterion 8 requires disclosure of author email addresses; only masked fragments (suffix of local part plus domain) are exposed, so the PII criterion is not met. Note: the endpoint is reachable unauthenticated and leaks UserId linkage and partial email suffixes, which may be reported separately as a lower-severity CWE-200 information-exposure observation, not as confirmed CWE-359.
